title: ACS Trace → OpenTelemetry semconv mapping
description: Normative mapping from ACS hooks and decisions to OpenTelemetry spans and span events. v0.1.0 conformance requires that a deployment emitting OTel for the Trace pillar uses these span names and required attributes verbatim. Decisions are recorded as span events on the parent step span, not as separate spans, so that the enforcement verdict and the action it gates share a parent and an OTel context.

step_to_span.description: Map ACS step methods to OTel span names and attributes. A required attribute's source field is required on the wire. A conditional attribute's source field is optional on the wire.

conditional_attributes.description: Attributes populated whenever the hook payload carries the source field. An exporter MUST emit each one when its source field is present and MUST omit it when the source field is absent. An empty source array counts as absent.

optional_attributes.description: Attributes an exporter MAY emit when its source field is present.

_note.description: Explanation for readers. The normative rules are in the lists and descriptions.

agbom/snapshot._note: acs.agbom.format names the AgBOM form the span records. No AgBOM payload carries a format field, because the wire form is always canonical. An exporter recording the payload sets canonical. A Guardian recording a serialization it rendered sets that serialization's agbom_serializations_supported value from the handshake.

agbom/changed._note: acs.agbom.format is sourced as on agbom/snapshot.

step_span_attributes.description: Attributes every step_to_span span carries in addition to its own entry's lists. acs.request_id is the step's own request_id, which every request envelope requires, so acs.request_id_ref on a steps/toolCallResult span joins to the steps/toolCallRequest span it reports on. The Observed Agent chooses request_id, and it is unique only within a session (Specification §10.3). A join MUST stay within one session, and two step spans in one session with the same acs.request_id are an integrity finding, not a join.

decision_event.description: Decisions are recorded as a span event named 'acs.decision' on the parent step span. The event MUST carry the disposition. It MUST carry each conditional attribute whenever the response carries the source field, and MUST omit it when the source field is absent. An empty source array counts as absent. The event records the Guardian's verdict, not the outcome the Observed Agent applied. When the same step span also carries an acs.decision.failure event, that event's acs.failure.posture is what the Observed Agent applied, and a reader MUST NOT count the acs.decision event as an enforced outcome. acs.reason_codes, acs.cited_provenance_ids and acs.chain_hash come from the response fields of the same name. acs.policy.ids, acs.policy.versions and acs.policy.rule_ids come from policy_references as three parallel string arrays. All three are emitted whenever the response carries a non-empty policy_references, and none is emitted otherwise. Each has the same length and order as policy_references, with an empty string where an entry lacks the field, so a reader can line up a policy, its version and its rule by position. An empty string on the wire cannot be told from an absent field, so a Guardian SHOULD NOT send one in a policy_references entry. acs.chain_hash is a copy of the response field, not a commitment on its own: the trace carries neither the response signature nor the ContextEntries a verifier needs (Specification §8.2, §8.6), and a Guardian's own trace is not an independent witness of its chain head.

decision_failure_event.description: A decision failure is recorded as a span event named 'acs.decision.failure' on the step span, separate from acs.decision. It records a step whose decision did not arrive or was not usable, and the failure posture applied instead. The Observed Agent MUST record every decision failure, fail-open or fail-closed, in the deployment's own audit log, and SHOULD emit this event when it claims ACS-Trace. A Guardian claiming ACS-Trace SHOULD emit it for the failures it sees itself: an error it returned (guardian_error) and a decision it finished after the negotiated timeout (timeout). In v0.1 the Observed Agent reports this event about its own conduct, so a missing event does not show that no failure happened, and a count built from these events is a lower bound. acs.failure.reported_by, acs.failure.posture and acs.failure.payload_bytes are the emitter's own claims. A failure count counts events reported by observed_agent, one per acs.request_id. Guardian events annotate those and are never added to the count, and a reader cross-checking the two sides takes them from separately produced streams. acs.failure.detail is required when acs.failure.class is other. It is free text that can echo request content, so it MUST NOT carry payload content, credentials or a raw response body. acs.failure.payload_bytes SHOULD be emitted, because when reported honestly it helps separate an induced failure from an organic one.

attribute_values.description: The values each enumerated attribute takes. timeout: the Guardian was reached and no decision arrived in time. unreachable: the request never reached the Guardian. malformed_response: an answer arrived and was not usable. guardian_error: an error came back instead of a decision. observed_agent_error: the Observed Agent's own side failed before a decision could arrive. other: a failure that fits none of these. acs.failure.posture is fail_open for on_decision_failure proceed and fail_closed for deny. A response that parses but breaks Specification §6.3 or §6.5 is not a decision failure, because those sections require the Observed Agent to apply DENY. malformed_response covers a response that does not parse or fails schema validation.

provenance_attributes.description: When Provenance is attached to a hook payload, the resulting span MUST carry provenance facts as attributes. Lineage edges MAY be linked via OTel span links keyed by provenance_id. v0.1 emits the factual provenance fields (origin, source_id) on the wire and on the span. Both are string arrays, also for a single Provenance object. acs.provenance.source_id has the same length and order as acs.provenance.origin, with an empty string where an object has no source_id. Trust classification is computed by the Guardian against local policy and is not a v0.1 span attribute (see §7.1).
